posterior transverse collateral sulcus: Posterior transverse branch of the collateral sulcus.
(communicating branch of median nerve wi: Connection between the median and ulnar nerves in the palm (a Riche–Cannieu-type anastomosis).
abducens nerve (vi): Supplies lateral rectus; because of its long course it is the nerve most often affected by raised intracranial pressure.
accessory nerve (xi): Supplies sternocleidomastoid and trapezius; being superficial in the posterior triangle, it can be injured in surgery (drooping shoulder).
accessory nucleus of oculomotor nerve: Parasympathetic nucleus supplying the pupillary sphincter and ciliary muscle (light and accommodation reflexes).
ampulla of lacrimal canaliculus: Dilatation at the end of the vertical part of the canaliculus.
amygdaloid body: Group of nuclei in the anteromedial temporal lobe; the centre of fear and emotional memory. Bilateral damage causes Klüver–Bucy syndrome.
angular gyrus: Gyrus capping the end of the superior temporal sulcus (Brodmann 39); linked to reading and writing; dominant-side damage causes Gerstmann syndrome.
anterior branch of medial antebrachial c: Anterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve
Supplies the skin of the anteromedial forearm.
anterior branch of obturator nerve: Supplies adductor longus, adductor brevis and gracilis, and the skin of the inner thigh.
anterior chamber of eyeball: Space between the cornea and the iris filled with aqueous humour; fluid drains at its angle (Schlemm's canal), and closure of the angle is acute glaucoma.
anterior cochlear nucleus: One of the first brainstem relay nuclei of the auditory fibres.
anterior commissure: Fibre bundle joining the temporal lobes and olfactory structures; it lies in the lamina terminalis.
anterior corticospinal tract: Uncrossed corticospinal fibres; they cross at segmental level and go to the trunk muscles.
anterior cutaneous branches of femoral n: Anterior cutaneous branches of femoral nerve
Sensation from the skin of the front and inner thigh.
anterior division of inferior trunk of b: Division that forms the medial cord.
anterior division of mandibular nerve: Mostly motor division; gives branches to the muscles of mastication and the buccal nerve.
anterior division of middle trunk of bra: Division that joins the lateral cord.
anterior division of superior trunk of b: Anterior division that joins the lateral cord.
anterior fasciculus proprius: Short fibres linking spinal cord segments (anterior funiculus).
anterior horn of spinal cord: Grey matter containing the lower motor neurons; damaged in poliomyelitis and ALS.
anterior interosseous nerve of forearm: Deep branch of the median nerve; supplies FPL, the radial half of FDP and pronator quadratus. After injury the 'OK' sign cannot be made.
anterior occipital sulcus*: Sulcus at the boundary of the occipital and temporal lobes.
anterior quadrangular lobule: Hemispheric part of the anterior lobe; part of the spinocerebellum.
anterior root of posterior femoral cutan: Anterior root of posterior femoral cutaneous nerve
Root of the nerve coming from the anterior divisions.
anterior root of spinal nerve: Root carrying motor and (at T1–L2 and S2–S4) autonomic fibres.
anterior segment of eyeball: Structures in front of the lens (cornea, anterior and posterior chambers, iris).
anterior spinocerebellar tract: Carries unconscious proprioception from the lower limb to the cerebellum through the superior cerebellar peduncle.
aqueduct of midbrain: Narrow canal joining the third and fourth ventricles; its obstruction causes obstructive hydrocephalus.
auditory tube: Connects the middle ear to the nasopharynx and equalises pressure; short and horizontal in children, so otitis media is common.
axillary nerve: Arises from the posterior cord, passes through the quadrangular space and winds around the surgical neck of the humerus; supplies deltoid and teres minor. Can be injured in shoulder dislocation and neck fracture (sensory loss over the 'badge' area).
base of peduncle: Anterior part of the midbrain carrying corticospinal and corticobulbar fibres; its damage causes contralateral hemiplegia in Weber syndrome.
biventral lobule: Two-bellied lobule of the inferior hemisphere.
branches of anterior part of lumbar plex: Branches of the anterior part of the lumbar plexus
branches of posterior part of lumbar ple: Branches of the posterior part of the lumbar plexus
buccal nerve: Carries sensation from the skin and mucosa of the cheek (not to be confused with the facial nerve branch supplying buccinator).
calcarine sulcus: Sulcus on the medial surface of the occipital lobe surrounded by the primary visual cortex (Brodmann 17). Posterior cerebral artery occlusion causes hemianopia with macular sparing.
cauda equina: Lumbar and sacral nerve roots descending from the conus medullaris; their compression causes incontinence and saddle anaesthesia and needs emergency surgery.
caudate nucleus: C-shaped basal nucleus following the lateral ventricle; it atrophies in Huntington disease.
central canal: Narrow canal in the middle of the spinal cord continuous with the fourth ventricle; its widening is syringomyelia.
central canal': Lower part of the central canal of the spinal cord.
central lobule: Middle part of the anterior lobe of the vermis.
central structures of spinal cord: Central structures of the spinal cord
central sulcus: Separates the frontal and parietal lobes, between the motor and sensory cortices.
chorda tympani: Branch of the facial nerve crossing the middle ear; it joins the lingual nerve and carries taste from the anterior two thirds of the tongue and parasympathetic fibres to the submandibular and sublingual glands.
choroid plexus: Vascular structure in the ventricles producing cerebrospinal fluid (about 500 ml a day).
cingulate gyrus (posteroventral part*): Part of the cingulate gyrus passing behind the splenium into the parahippocampal gyrus.
cingulate gyrus and sulcus (middle anter: Middle anterior part of the limbic gyrus above the corpus callosum; linked to attention and error monitoring.
cingulate gyrus and sulcus (middle poste: Middle posterior part of the cingulate gyrus.
cingulate gyrus and sulcus (posterior do: Posterior dorsal part of the cingulate gyrus.
cingulate sulcus (marginal part*): Upturned posterior end of the cingulate sulcus; it bounds the paracentral lobule behind.
cochlea: Organ of hearing coiled through 2.5 turns and containing the organ of Corti; its base detects high and its apex low frequencies.
cochlear nerve: Part carrying hearing information from the cochlea.
collateral sulcus: Sulcus on the inferior surface of the temporal lobe bounding the parahippocampal gyrus laterally.
commissural fibres of telencephalon: Fibres connecting the two cerebral hemispheres: the corpus callosum, anterior commissure and hippocampal commissure.
common fibular nerve: Lateral branch of the sciatic nerve; runs superficially around the neck of the fibula and is compressed by plaster casts or crossed legs, causing foot drop.
common palmar digital branches of median: Common palmar digital nerves of median nerve
Branches running in the palm towards the finger webs; they also supply the first two lumbricals.
common palmar digital branches of ulnar: Common palmar digital nerve of ulnar nerve
Branch running to the web between the ring and little fingers.
common plantar digital branches of later: Common plantar digital nerves of lateral plantar nerve
Branches running to the lateral toe webs.
common plantar digital branches of media: Common plantar digital nerves of medial plantar nerve
Branches running to the toe webs; compression between the 3rd and 4th metatarsals is Morton's neuroma.
cornea: Transparent anterior dome of the eye; avascular, it provides most of the refraction and is densely supplied by V1.
corpus callosum: Largest commissure joining the two hemispheres; it consists of rostrum, genu, body and splenium. When it is cut, 'split-brain' signs appear.
culmen: Highest vermian lobule of the anterior lobe.
cuneate fasciculus: Lateral dorsal column carrying the same senses from the upper trunk and arms (above T6).
cuneus: Triangular gyrus between the calcarine and parieto-occipital sulci; it represents the lower visual field.
declive: Vermian lobule behind the primary fissure.
deep branch of radial nerve: Motor branch piercing supinator to reach the posterior compartment of the forearm.
deep branch of ulnar nerve: Supplies the hypothenar, interosseous and 3rd–4th lumbrical muscles and adductor pollicis.
deep fibular nerve: Supplies the muscles of the anterior compartment and the skin between the 1st and 2nd toes.
dorsal branch of ulnar nerve: Carries sensation from the medial part of the back of the hand; it leaves before Guyon's canal, so it is spared in canal lesions.
dorsal digital branches of deep fibular: Dorsal digital nerves of deep fibular nerve
dorsal digital branches of radial nerve: Dorsal digital nerves of radial nerve
Sensation from the back of the lateral three and a half fingers (except the nail beds).
dorsal digital branches of superficial f: Dorsal digital nerves of superficial fibular nerve
Sensation from the dorsal surface of the toes.
dorsal digital branches of ulnar nerve: Dorsal digital nerves of ulnar nerve
Sensation from the back of the medial fingers.
